title: Antihistamine Relief Lag by Symptom
dataSources: Allergy symptoms (`allergy:entry`), migraine records (`migraine:entry`), bathroom visits (`bathroom:visit`), and sleep-talking events (`sleeptalk:event`).
app: Symptom telemetry for allergy diaries, migraine aura tracking, bathroom frequency logging, and sleep-talking review sent to Splunk HEC via apps and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=allergy:entry
| search relief_delay_min=*
| stats avg(relief_delay_min) as avg_relief_delay_min perc90(relief_delay_min) as p90_relief_delay_min count as samples by symptom_type
| sort 0 - avg_relief_delay_min
description: Measures antihistamine relief lag by symptom type.
value: Relief lag helps show which symptoms respond well and which may need a different strategy.
implementation: Send the relevant duration field for antihistamine relief lag to `index=personal` and review both average and p90 latency instead of relying on single examples.
visualization: Table of average and p90 antihistamine relief lag.
grandmaExplanation: It lists how long antihistamine relief lag usually takes, so slowdowns are obvious instead of anecdotal.
